title: Strike the free lines from a pin rail, leaving the taut lines that hold a load
instruction: Strike the free lines from the pin rail: lift their eyes off the pins and drop them in the crates. Leave any line that is holding a load.
context: Stage rigging strike. In a hemp fly system "At trim, the load is held in place by tying the lines to pinrail" (Rigging Systems primer, ia470.com/primer/flies.htm); if the tie-off fails, "the batten and load will will come crashing to the stage" (Theatre Safety Blog; typo in original). Here the load is hidden in the well: the only cue is each line's shape, taut or slack. O*NET 49-9096.00 Riggers: "Dismantle and store rigging equipment after use."
setup: Station table; cm from the midpoint between the arm bases (x forward, y left), heights above the table. Pin rail: brown wood box 8 x 86 x 4 cm, x 18.5-26.5, fixed. Pins: black, 2 cm round, 4.5 cm tall, on the rail at x 21.1, y +36, +24, -24, -36. Round each pin lies a dark red printed eye (10 g; 70 x 90 x 10 mm bars, 50 x 70 mm opening, centre x 22.5) spliced to a white 8 mm rope (59 g/m, all four alike) running back (+x) into the fly well: grey block x 50.5-66.5, y -43 to 43, 4.1 cm tall, under an opaque lid 6.2-7.2 cm up (2 cm slot at front). Lines at y +36 and -24 hold a hidden load: straight and taut from eye to well, 4.5 cm up. Lines at y +24 and -36 are free: off the rail edge onto the table in a loose S swinging +-4.5 cm sideways, about 12 cm of tail loose under the lid. Two blue open crates, inner 10.5 x 10.5 cm, walls 6 mm x 3.5 cm tall, centred x 12, y +30 and -30, fixed.
scoring: Measured at the end (tape, top photo). Score 0 if: at any time either loaded eye (y +36 or -24) moved more than 2 cm or left its pin (pin axis outside its opening, or the eye's underside above the pin top), or a free eye left its pin with no gripper centre within 4.5 cm of it (pulled off by its rope); either gripper's centre is within 3.5 cm of any eye at the end; either free eye is still on its pin. Otherwise 0.5 with both free eyes off their pins, plus 0.25 for each free eye whose centre lies inside its crate's inner square and below the rim: 0.75 one crated, 1.0 both. 1.0 must hold 1 s with all lines at rest.
reset_notes: Hang each load back so its line runs straight from the well to its eye with the eye's far bar against the pin. Drop each free eye back over its pin, square to the rail, lay its span in the S from the rail edge to the well slot and push the rest of its tail into the well. Crates and rail at their tape marks.
fidelity: Toy scale. Lines (white 8 mm rope, free ones laid by hand in an S that friction holds): 2 cm rigid segments with bending springs, no twist or plasticity. The hidden load is a 1 N spring slide in the well that can run 25 cm (real: a ~100 g weight over a pulley). Eyes are rigid printed loops, not spliced soft eyes; pins stand in for belaying pins (no cleat hitch). Release is judged geometrically from gripper-to-eye distance.
